title: Group 2 Mains Paper II · Challenge drill
provenance: Original GateLabs questions informed by the published exam pattern. Pattern reference: https://portal-psc.ap.gov.in/HomePages/KeysToPapers
note: Original quantitative economy questions and applied science and technology cases, based on the two Paper II syllabus blocks.

questions.subject: Indian and Andhra Pradesh Economy
questions.question: A budget shows total expenditure of ₹8,200 crore, revenue receipts of ₹6,500 crore, non-debt capital receipts of ₹450 crore and interest payments of ₹620 crore. What is its primary deficit?
options: ₹630 crore
₹1,080 crore
₹1,250 crore
₹1,870 crore
questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit is 8,200−6,500−450 = 1,250. Primary deficit subtracts the interest bill: 1,250−620 = 630 crore.

questions.subject: Indian and Andhra Pradesh Economy
questions.question: Andhra Pradesh’s hypothetical nominal GSDP rises by 12.2% while the GSDP deflator rises by 10%. What is real GSDP growth?
questions.explanation: Divide nominal growth factor by the deflator factor: 1.122/1.10 = 1.02. Subtract 1 to obtain 2%.

questions.subject: Indian and Andhra Pradesh Economy
questions.question: At current prices, aggregate gross value added at basic prices is ₹900 crore, product taxes ₹110 crore, product subsidies ₹30 crore and consumption of fixed capital ₹80 crore. What is net domestic product at market prices?
options: ₹820 crore
₹870 crore
₹900 crore
₹980 crore
questions.explanation: GDP at market prices is GVA plus net product taxes, or 980. Subtract consumption of fixed capital of 80 for net domestic product of 900.

questions.subject: Indian and Andhra Pradesh Economy
questions.question: During a quarter, a hypothetical economy’s goods balance is −40, services balance +25, primary income balance −7, secondary income balance +10, and net inward FDI 30, all in identical units. What is the current-account balance?
questions.explanation: The current account is −40+25−7+10 = −12. FDI belongs to the financial account.

questions.subject: Indian and Andhra Pradesh Economy
questions.question: In an economy, agriculture contributes 18% of GVA and employs 45% of workers. Services contribute 54% of GVA and employ 30% of workers. What is services GVA per worker as a multiple of agricultural GVA per worker?
questions.explanation: Relative to economy-wide GVA per worker, the ratios are 54/30 = 1.8 and 18/45 = 0.4. Dividing gives 4.5.

questions.subject: Indian and Andhra Pradesh Economy
questions.question: Assume banks’ loan rates are linked one-for-one to the policy repo rate and savings deposit rates remain fixed for a year. With loan principal unchanged, a repo rate cut would immediately do what?
options: Reduce nominal interest on linked loans and narrow the spread over savings rates
Raise linked loan payments and narrow the spread
Keep linked loan payments fixed and widen the spread
Reduce loan rates and widen the spread over unchanged savings rates
questions.explanation: Linked loan rates fall by the amount of the cut. Since savings rates remain fixed, the loan–savings spread narrows by the same amount.

questions.subject: Indian and Andhra Pradesh Economy
questions.question: A crop has a declared MSP of ₹2,250 per quintal. In district A, procurement buys at that rate and farmers can sell immediately. In district B, farmers sell at a local market price of ₹2,080 and lack access to procurement. Which conclusion follows?
options: All B farmers receive the difference automatically because MSP is declared
The declared price lifts the observed B market price to at least ₹2,250
Procurement access can cause different realised prices despite an identical national MSP
B’s MSP is ₹2,080 since that is the observed market price
questions.explanation: The MSP is a declared benchmark. Effective procurement at the price can change the amount farmers realise. No payment mechanism for B is specified.

questions.subject: Science and Technology
questions.question: A 120 MW solar park runs at a 25% capacity factor over a year of 8,760 hours. Twenty per cent of its energy is routed through storage with 75% round-trip efficiency. The rest is delivered directly. How much electricity reaches the grid?
questions.explanation: Generation is 120×8760×0.25 = 262.8 GWh. The delivered share is 0.80+0.20×0.75 = 0.95, giving 249.66 GWh.

questions.subject: Science and Technology
questions.question: An inlet has BOD 240 mg/L. A primary step removes 30% of the incoming BOD and a secondary step removes 85% of the BOD reaching that step. Assume flow is unchanged. What is the final BOD?
questions.explanation: Each removal percentage applies to its own inlet. The final fraction is 0.70×0.15 = 0.105. Multiply by 240 to obtain 25.2 mg/L.

questions.subject: Science and Technology
questions.question: A proposed conservation plan banks several crop varieties and also protects the wild relatives in their native habitat. Which distinction is correct?
options: The seed bank is in situ because varieties come from the region
The seed bank is ex situ while native habitat protection is in situ
Both measures are ex situ because human intervention is involved
Habitat protection is ex situ if threatened species are monitored
questions.explanation: In situ conservation maintains populations within natural habitats. Storing seeds in a managed collection outside those habitats is ex situ.

questions.subject: Science and Technology
questions.question: Which combination was demonstrated during the April 2025 SpaDeX experiments? I. Autonomous closing and docking from the final approach. II. Bidirectional electrical power transfer while docked. III. Debris capture and deorbiting.
options: I and II only
I and III only
II and III only
I, II and III
questions.explanation: ISRO reported a fully autonomous final approach during the second docking and power transfer in both directions the following day.

questions.subject: Science and Technology
questions.question: When additional atmospheric CO₂ dissolves in seawater, what change most directly makes calcium carbonate formation more difficult, all else equal?
options: Higher pH and a rise in carbonate ions
Lower pH and a decline in available carbonate ions
Lower pH and an increase in available carbonate ions
A decline in dissolved carbon dioxide and no change in pH
questions.explanation: Dissolved CO₂ increases hydrogen ion concentration. Hydrogen ions combine with carbonate to form bicarbonate, reducing carbonate available for shell formation.

questions.subject: Science and Technology
questions.question: Among 10,000 people, 2% have a condition. A screening test has sensitivity 90% and specificity 95%. Assuming exactly these rates, what fraction of positive results are true positives?
questions.explanation: Of 200 affected people, 180 test positive. Of 9,800 unaffected, 490 test positive. The fraction is 180/(180+490) = 18/67.

questions.subject: Science and Technology
questions.question: A transport inventory finds that a fuel-quality change reduced exhaust sulfur dioxide between two surveys, while roadside coarse particulate matter stayed high. Which interpretation is best supported?
options: Lower exhaust sulfur dioxide proves all particulate sources declined
Fuel sulfur and coarse particles must respond in the same proportion
Road dust and other non-exhaust sources can sustain coarse particulate levels despite lower exhaust sulfur dioxide
Coarse particulate matter directly measures only tailpipe sulfur releases
questions.explanation: Emitted sulfur dioxide responds to fuel sulfur, whereas coarse particles can come from resuspended dust and wear. Their trends can therefore diverge.
